 by Cricbuzz Staff •     Share Tweet India won the 5th ODI to clinch the series 3-1 © AFP India won the 5th ODI to clinch the series 3-1 © AFP India have been fined 35 per cent of their match fees for their slow over-rate during the fifth ODI of the series against New Zealand.
 Led by Shreyas Iyer, India were found to be seven overs short, even after time allowances were taken into consideration. Iyer, leading in the absence of regular ODI captain Shubman Gill for the last two games, accepted the sanction put forth by match referee Ranjan Madugalle.
 India claimed the series 3-1, finishing with a 22-run win after defending 209 in Mount Maunganui.
 The players were fined five per cent of their match fees for every over they fell short of the target, which is capped at a maximum of 50 per cent, as per Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct on Players and Player Support Personnel.
 Last month, India were also sanctioned for slow over-rate during the West Indies ODI series at home, and were docked 20 per cent of their match fees in Mullanpur. Before that, India’s last sanction came in December 2025, after an ODI against South Africa in Raipur.
